sonnet.problem: The question says the high priest charges Jesus under oath 'so' the witnesses haven't given the council what it wants. That adds a reason for the charge. Matthew 26:63 never says why the high priest swears Jesus in.
sonnet.rule: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

sonnet.problem: The story card says the people nearby 'have been hearing him talk'. That hands the baker the answer to the very next card, which asks what gives Peter away (his accent). It also adds a detail the text doesn't state.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Card 6 has just said the council is looking for false testimony. Card 7 then asks whether false witnesses give it 'the testimony it's looking for'. A thoughtful baker would reason True, because false witnesses give false testimony, yet the answer is False. The only way to get it right is luck or knowing the verse.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
